purpose: Expansion corpus of relevant lolcow / Farm-adjacent figures for comparative research. Inclusion means documented relevance to the lolcow/Farm cultural category, not a judgment of character or truth of every community allegation.
epistemic_rule: Community labels are recorded as community classifications. Claims about misconduct require separate evidence records and are not established by inclusion here.
source_note: Know Your Meme's lolcow guide explicitly identifies Chris Chan, JustinRPG, Terry Davis and Onision among prominent examples, while its Lolcow Live entry documents a contemporary ecosystem involving Boogie2988, WingsOfRedemption and farmer-side creators. A 2020 Know Your Meme lolcow image also indexes a wider historical cluster.

figures.name: Onision
figures.why_relevant: One of the older large-scale YouTube controversy subjects repeatedly cited in lolcow culture; useful for studying how creator fame becomes a durable archive.
figures.evidence_status: category relevance documented; individual allegations require separate case files

figures.name: DarkSydePhil
figures.why_relevant: Long-running gaming creator who became a recurring subject of reaction, commentary and the proposed Lolcow Live ecosystem.

figures.name: WingsOfRedemption
figures.why_relevant: A clear case of the Cow/Farmer boundary becoming porous: he is both a subject of long-running commentary and a participant in Lolcow Live.

figures.name: Boogie2988
figures.why_relevant: Important modern example because the subject is also commercially embedded in the Farm: Lolcow Live turns the subject/farmer relationship into a formal media product.

figures.name: Keemstar
figures.why_relevant: Useful not simply as a Cow but as infrastructure: he is associated with the production and monetization of drama-oriented media and Lolcow Live.

figures.name: Nicholas DeOrio
figures.why_relevant: Represents the commentary/farmer side of the contemporary ecosystem, including participation around Lolcow Live.

figures.name: SomeOrdinaryGamers
figures.why_relevant: Useful comparison case: commentary can intersect with Farm economics while retaining a broader technology/investigation identity.

figures.name: Tommy C
figures.why_relevant: Part of the farmer-side ecosystem documented around Lolcow Live's development.

figures.name: Turkey Tom
figures.why_relevant: Useful for studying how commentary creators become recognizable nodes in the Farm rather than anonymous audience members.

figures.name: Quinton Reviews
figures.why_relevant: Named in historical lolcow-culture indexes; useful for examining the boundary between long-form creator commentary and Farm culture.

figures.name: MundaneMatt
figures.why_relevant: Historical example from the commentary ecosystem that helps map the transition between conventional creator criticism and Farm culture.

figures.name: Spoony
figures.why_relevant: Useful historical case for studying how an early Internet creator can accumulate a long tail of community memory and criticism.

figures.name: The Amazing Atheist
figures.why_relevant: Named in historical lolcow culture indexes and useful for studying political/ideological commentary intersecting with personality-driven attention.

figures.name: LowTierGod
figures.why_relevant: Useful case of competitive gaming personality, livestream conflict and recurring reaction content becoming an enduring meme/archive subject.

figures.name: Nikocado Avocado
figures.why_relevant: Important case for studying deliberate spectacle, transformation narratives, audience retention and the boundary between self-produced spectacle and Farm consumption.

figures.name: CopperCab
figures.why_relevant: Early viral-era example useful for comparing pre-algorithmic and algorithmic Farm dynamics.

figures.name: Andrew Dobson
figures.why_relevant: Included in historical lolcow culture indexes; useful as an archival case rather than a current status claim.

figures.name: Ethan Ralph
figures.why_relevant: Useful for studying the point where the producer of drama becomes an object of drama himself.

figures.name: Zoe Quinn
figures.why_relevant: Useful for studying how a political-cultural controversy can become a durable networked archive rather than a conventional lolcow case.
figures.evidence_status: category relevance documented; allegations require individual sourcing

figures.name: Brianna Wu
figures.why_relevant: Useful comparative case for studying harassment, political visibility and long-lived Internet archives without collapsing those phenomena into lolcow status.

figures.name: Ethan Klein
figures.why_relevant: Useful for studying movement between commentary, celebrity, controversy and being a subject of other commentary.

figures.name: Lily Orchard
figures.why_relevant: Useful for studying how long-form criticism can itself become the object of criticism and archive-building.

figures.name: Mister Metokur
figures.why_relevant: Useful for studying the farmer-side production infrastructure and how commentators can become major nodes in the same ecosystem they document.

figures.name: Chris-chan
figures.why_relevant: Core long-duration case for the entire research model: repeated public output, trolling, documentation, dedicated encyclopedia and persistent archival memory.

figures.name: JustinRPG
figures.why_relevant: One of the examples explicitly named in Know Your Meme's general lolcow history; useful for the early pre-platformization period.

figures.name: Terry A. Davis
figures.why_relevant: Important because his case demonstrates how technical work, unusual public communication, mental-health narratives and Internet mythmaking can combine into a long-lived archive. Treat sensitive details carefully and avoid using diagnosis as ridicule.

figures.name: Amberlynn Reid
figures.why_relevant: Long-running YouTube subject useful for studying audience participation, weight/lifestyle narratives, relationship cycles and reaction content.

figures.name: Foodie Beauty
figures.why_relevant: Useful cross-border case for examining mukbang, lifestyle streaming, relationship narratives and audience reaction loops.

figures.name: KingCobraJFS
figures.why_relevant: Important long-running case combining genuine fans, critics, livestreaming, lifestyle content and a substantial archive; demonstrates that a Farm subject can have authentic supporters and creative output.

figures.name: MusicBizMarty
figures.why_relevant: Especially valuable for the model because the actor can occupy both sides of the Farm: creating material about another subject while becoming an archived subject himself.

figures.name: Daniel Larson
figures.why_relevant: A contemporary short-form-video case with a large dedicated wiki, making it useful for comparing TikTok-era Farm formation with older forum-era cases.

figures.name: Cyraxx
figures.why_relevant: Useful for long-running forum-centered attention, reaction cycles and exceptionally large discussion archives.

figures.name: Tophiachu
figures.why_relevant: Useful contemporary case for studying how TikTok, livestreams and rapid reposting produce newer Farm dynamics.
figures.evidence_status: category relevance documented; individual claims require sourcing

next_fields.important_principle: Do not score people by 'lolcow severity'. Score the measurable structure of the ecosystem: duration, archive density, participant count, cross-platform spread, reaction velocity, monetization and persistence.
